A 3-hour maximum value resulting from plume impaction on the Little Wolf Mountains approximately 16 kilometers north-northeast through southeast of the proposed facility was computed. The maximum "worst" case 3-hour SO<sub>2</sub> average concentration using the methodology from Appendix J was computed at abut 800 ug/m<sup>3</sup>. This is safely below the state and federal standards but is above the Class II allowable 3-hour SO<sub>2</sub> increment level.
Maximum 24-hour calculated concentrations for SO<sub>2</sub> and particulates were all well below the federal and state standards and, with the exception of the 24-hour impaction model, all were safely below the Class II allowable increment levels. The 24-hour impaction calculations indicated a maximum SO<sub>2</sub> value of about 100 ug/m<sup>3</sup> or the equivalent of Class II 24-hour allowable increment.
The CO<sub>2</sub> Acceptor process has given indications of being considerably more efficient than the Lurgi gasification process, and therefore should produce somewhat fewer airborne pollutants per million cubic feet of gas produced. For the Lurgi process, the quantities emmitted are considerably less than for a conventional power generating plant.
A recent report on the newer processes seems to confirm this claim. Research and development work by the El Paso Gas Company, (1973) indicates that the quantity of
